title: God Is Working for Your Good
story:
A young boy loved building things with small blocks.

One afternoon, he decided to build a tall tower. He carefully placed one block on top of another, trying to make it as high as possible.

But just when he was almost finished, the tower suddenly fell apart.

The boy became disappointed and said, "All my work is wasted."

His father sat beside him and said, "It is not wasted. We can use these same pieces to build something even better."

Together they looked at the fallen blocks and began again.

This time, the father helped him build a stronger foundation. The new tower was not exactly what the boy had originally imagined, but it was stronger and more stable.

The boy realized that what looked like failure had become part of something better.

Romans 8:28 reminds us that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him and are called according to His purpose.

This does not mean that everything that happens to us is good.

Some experiences are painful.

Some disappointments are difficult to understand.

Some prayers seem unanswered, and some seasons of life may leave us wondering why God allowed certain things to happen.

Yet God can work through all these circumstances for His good purpose.

He can take situations that appear broken and bring something meaningful from them.

He can use difficulties to develop patience, disappointments to deepen our faith, and closed doors to lead us toward a different path.

Sometimes we can see what God was doing only after many years have passed.

At the moment, all we may see is a broken piece of the story.

But God sees the whole picture.

Imagine looking at the back of a beautifully woven piece of cloth. From the back, you may see tangled threads crossing in different directions.

It may look confusing and unfinished.

But when you turn it around, you see a beautiful design that the person weaving it could see all along.

Our lives can sometimes feel like those tangled threads.

We see individual events and wonder how they could possibly fit together.

God sees the complete picture.

When Paul wrote Romans 8:28, he was not promising believers a life without trouble. The surrounding passage speaks about suffering, weakness, hope, and perseverance.

The promise is deeper: God is able to work through every circumstance according to His purpose.

This gives us hope when life does not make sense.

If you are going through disappointment today, do not conclude that God has abandoned you.

If a door has closed, do not assume that your story is finished.

If something you prayed for has not happened, continue trusting God even while you wait.

You may not understand what He is doing today, but you can trust His character.

God's definition of good may also be greater than our definition of comfort.

Sometimes we ask God to make our circumstances easier, while He is using those circumstances to make us stronger, wiser, more compassionate, and more like Christ.

His purpose is not simply to give us everything we want. His purpose is to shape our lives according to His will.

Therefore, when you face something difficult, bring it honestly to God.

Tell Him about your pain.

Ask Him for wisdom.

Ask Him to show you what you can learn.

And then trust Him with what you cannot understand.

The chapter you are living today may not make sense yet.

But God is still working.

The pieces may look scattered, but He knows how to put them together.

The road may look different from what you expected, but He can still lead you toward His purpose.

So keep praying.

Keep trusting.

Keep walking faithfully.

One day you may look back and recognize how God used even the difficult parts of your journey for His good purpose.

Until then, remember this: you do not have to understand everything to trust the One who does.
life_lesson: Not everything that happens in life is good, but God can work through every circumstance for the good of those who love Him and live according to His purpose. Trust Him even when you cannot yet see how everything will come together.
prayer:
Dear Heavenly Father,

Thank You for the promise that You are working through all things for the good of those who love You and are called according to Your purpose.

When life does not make sense, help me trust You instead of becoming discouraged.

When I experience disappointment, remind me that my story is not finished.

When something I hoped for does not happen, give me patience to wait and faith to continue trusting You.

Help me remember that You see the complete picture when I can see only a small part of it.

Use my difficult experiences to strengthen my faith, develop my character, and make me more like Christ.

Give me wisdom to learn from every season of my life.

When doors close, help me believe that You can lead me toward the right path.

When I experience pain, comfort my heart and remind me that You have not abandoned me.

Help me surrender the things I cannot understand and trust Your wisdom and goodness.

Teach me not to measure Your goodness only by how comfortable my circumstances are.

Help me recognize the ways You are shaping me even through challenges.

Give me courage to keep praying, keep trusting, and keep walking faithfully.

When I cannot see what You are doing, help me trust who You are.

Thank You for being faithful even when I do not understand Your plans.

Take every part of my life and use it according to Your good and perfect purpose.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
reflection_question:
What difficult situation in your life is hardest for you to understand right now?

Can you trust God with that situation even before you see how He will work through it?

What might God be teaching or developing in you through the circumstances you are facing today?
verse: And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love Him, who have been called according to His purpose.
